description: Rainfall is one of the most important climatic factors affecting crop growth, irrigation scheduling, fertilizer application, pest incidence, and overall agricultural productivity.

types_of_rainfall.name: Convectional Rainfall
types_of_rainfall.description: Occurs due to heating of the earth's surface.

types_of_rainfall.name: Orographic Rainfall
types_of_rainfall.description: Occurs when moist air rises over mountains.

types_of_rainfall.name: Cyclonic Rainfall
types_of_rainfall.description: Occurs due to cyclones and low-pressure systems.

during_rain: Prevent livestock from entering flooded areas.

crop_specific_advisory.Rice: Maintain standing water only as recommended; avoid prolonged flooding.
crop_specific_advisory.Maize: Drain excess water immediately to prevent root damage.
crop_specific_advisory.Wheat: Avoid waterlogging during flowering and grain filling.
crop_specific_advisory.Tomato: Ensure proper drainage to reduce fungal diseases.

impact_on_fertilizers: Heavy rain may wash away fertilizers.
Avoid urea application before heavy rainfall.
Split fertilizer doses during rainy season.
impact_on_pests_and_diseases: Rainfall may reduce some insect populations but increase others.

faqs.question: Should fertilizers be applied before heavy rainfall?
faqs.answer: No. Heavy rainfall can wash away fertilizers, reducing their effectiveness.

faqs.question: What should farmers do after heavy rain?
faqs.answer: Drain excess water, inspect crops for diseases, and apply recommended plant protection measures if needed.

faqs.question: How does rainfall affect crop diseases?
faqs.answer: High humidity and prolonged leaf wetness encourage fungal and bacterial diseases.

faqs.question: How can excess rainwater be managed?
faqs.answer: Construct drainage channels, farm ponds, and rainwater harvesting structures.
